ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High-contrast distribution; approximately 70% high-intensity white/cream pixels concentrated in the central lobe regions versus 30% low-intensity black pixels localized at the trailing edges and peduncle insertion.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Large contiguous white focal zones occupy the central and inner areas of both lobes. Black pigmentation forms a continuous band along the trailing edge, widening significantly towards the distal tips and the median notch. Small, low-intensity elliptical spots are scattered across the white regions.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Distinct V-shaped notch with a calculated interior angle of approximately 48 degrees; depth is deep relative to the fluke width.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Highly irregular serration pattern. The left lobe trailing edge displays high-amplitude, jagged peaks with deep valleys. The right lobe displays a more moderate frequency of serration with lower peak amplitudes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: The leading edges follow a sharp convex curve tapering to acute, pointed distal tips. The trailing edges exhibit a generally concave sweep towards the median notch.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Dense, three-dimensional clusters of high-contrast, brownish-white calcified organisms (barnacles) are localized on the distal tips and the leading edge of the left lobe.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Multiple dark, unaligned linear pixel disruptions (rake marks) are visible on the white ventral surface of both lobes, particularly three parallel diagonal marks on the mid-left lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Prominent tooth-rake scars likely from predator interaction on the ventral surface; heavy barnacle colonization (Coronula diadema) altering the geometric silhouette of the fluke tips.
other_distinctive_markers: Extensive high-intensity specular highlights (glimmer) from water droplets across the lower third of the fluke surface, partially obscuring fine pigmentation detail near the peduncle.
